description: Words whose British and American senses differ, plus domain lexis where the American reader would misparse the British term. Merges the semantic slice (same spelling, different meaning; pragmatics and register) with the domain slice (food, clothing, transport, house, school, health, work, sport, objects). Sides are authored, not slot-substituted: many contrasts are sense explanations.

excluded_claims.fag-is-common: Dated/regional cigarette sense is taught only as quoted interpretation; the word is a severe anti-gay slur in other contexts.
excluded_claims.nappy-hair-neutral: The US hair sense is racialised and can be offensive; it is explained only as a warning, never elicited as ordinary vocabulary.
excluded_claims.public-school-all-uk: The elite fee-paying sense is chiefly England/Wales and must not be projected onto every UK education system.
excluded_claims.date-without-locale: A bare numeric date is not labelled correct without an explicit locale.
excluded_claims.tone-as-universal: Pragmatic readings are presented as common tendencies with contextual evidence, not rules about every speaker.

excluded_claims_note: Statements the authoring deliberately refuses to teach. Safety carve-outs, not oversights.
overlap_note: Ten concepts are authored in both slices and six more duplicate an expression entry. Both authorings are kept — they are different sentences — and cross-linked via also_covered_by.
